raw_response:
I will keep my planting simple and stable this year. In Quzhou County, the wheat-maize rotation fits my land, water conditions, machinery, and labor best, and at my age I do not want to spread myself across too many crops. I will use the same 30 mu for a full winter wheat followed by summer maize rotation. I am educated and I pay attention to input efficiency, so I will use improved seed, control fertilizer rates instead of chasing yield blindly, irrigate only at the key stages, and rely on rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season. For wheat, I will focus on strong establishment, one good topdressing, and disease control around the main risk periods. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize quickly to protect the growing season, keep the stand uniform, and manage water and pests conservatively but on time. I am choosing reliability, manageable labor, and steady output over experimentation this year.
